name: Gwama
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Andargachew Getu Gebeyehu. 2021. [Long grammar of Gwama, 310 pp; Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description, Addis Ababa]. Also Zelealem Leyew 2005 grammar. Neither found online.

sources.citation: Zelealem Leyew. 2005. Gwama, a little-known endangered language of Ethiopia: a sketch of its grammar and lexicon. Addis Ababa University, Dept. of Linguistics. 39 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.4 Tone (p. 7): 'Gwama is a tonal language with rising and falling tone levels' with H/L minimal pairs; sec. 2.5 syllable structure; interrogative intonation noted (p. ~25). No stress statement.

sources.citation: Leyew, Zelealem (n.d.). Gwama, a little-known endangered language of Ethiopia: a sketch of its grammar and lexicon. Addis Ababa University: Dep. of Linguistics. 39 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Not in catalog; no existing statements. The work is silent on stress; it only describes lexical tone and interrogative intonation.

sources.citation: Kievit, Dirk & Erika Robertson. 2012. Notes on Gwama grammar. Studies in African Linguistics 41(1): 39-97.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 'Notes on phonology' (pp. 41-42) gives consonant/vowel inventory and reports, after Hellenthal & Kutsch Lojenga (2011), three contrastive level tones (H, M, L) plus rising and falling; lexical tone minimal sets. No mention of stress.

sources.citation: Andargachew Getu Gebeyehu. 2026. Clause combining in Gwama. University of Nairobi Journal of Language and Linguistics 12: 100-118.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; 'Tone and ATR are not considered in this work.' Useful for its bibliography (cites Gebeyehu 2019 phonology, 2021 PhD, Goldberg 2018 grammar guide, Hellenthal & Kutsch Lojenga 2011).

sources.citation: Andargachew Getu Gebeyehu. 2025. Nominal and verbal modification in Gwama. Aethiopica 28: 162-180.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; morphosyntax only (tone marked on associative -á).

sources.citation: Andargachew Getu Gebeyehu. 2021. Documentation and grammatical description of Gwama. PhD dissertation, Addis Ababa University. 310 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only full grammar (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description); its phonology chapter (expanding the author's 2019 article) is the most likely place for an explicit statement on stress/accent or its absence.

sources.citation: Andargachew Getu Gebeyehu. 2019. A phonology of Gwama. International Journal of Research in Social Sciences and Humanities (IJRSSH) 9(2): 356-382.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Dedicated 27-pp phonology (consonants, vowels, ATR harmony, length, sec. 4 Tone pp. 374-375: three contrastive level tones H/M/L, noun and verb melodies; sec. 5 syllable structure; morphophonemics). The word 'stress' does not occur; no statement on accent/prominence.

sources.citation: Otero, Manuel A. 2019. A historical reconstruction of the Koman language family. PhD dissertation, University of Oregon. 756 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Gwama phonological sketch sec. 2.1.4 (pp. 40-47, Highland and Lowland Gwama, own fieldwork + Hellenthal & Kutsch Lojenga 2011, Goldberg et al. 2017); sec. 2.1.4.4 'Gwama Tone' p. 47: three level tones L/M/H plus rising; 'no significant tonal processes.. nor is there downstepping or downdrifting'. 'stress' occurs nowhere in the dissertation.

sources.citation: Siebert, Ralph, Kati Siebert & Klaus Wedekind. 2002. Sociolinguistic survey report on languages of the Asosa-Begi-Komosha area, Part I. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-054.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistics + 320-item Kwama wordlist with impressionistic tone marks ('a partial analysis of tonal systems will be published separately').

sources.citation: Wedekind, Klaus & Charlotte Wedekind. 2002. Sociolinguistic survey report of the Asosa-Begi-Komosha area, Part II. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-055.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Its sound-inventory sections (4, 5) cover Northern Mao and Berta, not Kwama; Kwama appears only in the comparative wordlist. Nothing on Gwama stress.
